# GitHub Webhooks: integration analysis

> Generated by API Integration Scout from <https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks> on 2026-10-27T16:09:50.094Z.
> Every finding is marked **Documented** (quoted from the docs and verified), **Inferred** (the agent's reasoning) or **Not found in docs**.

**Goal:** Receive GitHub issue-opened webhooks on a Node.js server, verify the webhook signature, and extract the issue title, author and link from the payload to post a message to a team chat.

This analysis covers only what the goal needs.

GitHub webhooks send HTTP POST deliveries to your server when events such as issue activity occur. You configure the payload URL, content type, secret and events in repository, organization or GitHub App settings. Each delivery is signed with an HMAC SHA-256 header that your server should verify.

## At a glance

| Area | Finding | Status | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base URL | — | Not found in docs | — |
| Authentication | other: Inbound webhook authentication: set a secret on the webhook. GitHub signs each delivery with HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, sent as 'sha256=<hexdigest>' in X-Hub-Signature-256. Your server recomputes and compares using a constant-time comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual in Node.js). (+1 documented alternative) | Documented | [/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries) |
| Pagination | — | Not found in docs | — |
| Rate limits | — | Not found in docs | — |
| Webhooks | Yes: issues (action: opened, among others), ping | Documented | [/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads), [/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks) |
| Error format | — | Not found in docs | — |

| Endpoints | 0 found | 0 documented, 0 inferred | — |

## Integration flow

1. **Create a repository or organization webhook in Settings > Webhooks with Payload URL, content type application/json, a high-entropy secret, and the Issues event** (Your app → API). Documented: [/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks)
2. **Store the secret securely on your server (for example in an environment variable)** (on your side). Documented: [/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries)
3. **GitHub sends a ping event after the webhook is created** (API → your webhook). Documented: [/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks)
4. **When an issue is opened, GitHub POSTs an issues event (action: opened) with signature headers** (API → your webhook). Documented: [/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads)
5. **Verify the signature: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the secret, compare to X-Hub-Signature-256 with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and reject on mismatch** (on your side). Documented: [/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries)
6. **Check X-GitHub-Event == issues and action == opened, then read the issue title, author login and issue URL from the payload, and post a message to the team chat** (on your side). Inferred: [/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads)

The diagram is in `sequence.mmd`.

## Risks

- **HIGH**: Must verify against the raw body. If Express parses the JSON before you hash it, re-serialization changes the bytes and the signature fails. Use express.raw or capture the raw body. Compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual.
- **MEDIUM**: Content type. With application/x-www-form-urlencoded the JSON arrives in a 'payload' form parameter. Choose application/json.
- **MEDIUM**: No signature header if no secret. X-Hub-Signature-256 is sent only when a secret is configured. Reject unsigned requests.
- **MEDIUM**: Issue field names not confirmed from the page. The page I read abbreviates the issue object. issue.title, issue.user.login and issue.html_url come from my knowledge of the payload, not from the pages I fetched. Check them against a real delivery.
- **LOW**: Ghost sender. sender may be the 'ghost' placeholder user in some cases.
- **LOW**: Respond quickly, redelivery. I did not read the timeout and redelivery details. Check the handling-deliveries page. Dedupe on X-GitHub-Delivery.
- **LOW**: Public endpoint. The server needs a publicly reachable HTTPS URL, or a reverse proxy or the CLI forwarder for local testing.

## Open questions

- What is the response timeout for deliveries, and how does redelivery work (handling-webhook-deliveries page, not read)?
- What are the exact field names of the issue object (title, user.login, html_url)? The schema was collapsed on the page I read.
- Does the team chat have its own incoming-webhook API? That is outside this goal and not covered here.

### Webhooks

- Supported: yes
- Events: `issues (action: opened, among others)`, `ping`
- Signature verification: Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body with your secret, prefix it with 'sha256=', and compare to X-Hub-Signature-256 using crypto.timingSafeEqual. Handle the payload as UTF-8. Do not use ==. Verification needs the unparsed raw body, for example from express.raw.
- Create a repository or organization webhook (or a GitHub App webhook), subscribe to the Issues event, and choose application/json so the body is the raw JSON. Payloads are capped at 25 MB. GitHub sends a ping event after you create the webhook.

Payload fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string | The action performed, e.g. opened |
| `issue` | object | The issue itself (required) |
| `repository` | object | The repository where the event occurred (required) |
| `sender` | object | The GitHub user who triggered the event (required). May be the 'ghost' user. |
| `organization` | object | Present for organization webhooks or org-owned repos |
| `installation` | object | Present when sent to a GitHub App |

```
...
},

}
}
```
